C: B1 a glass or clay container with a wide opening at the top and sometimes a fitted lid, usually used for storing food
› UK informal a drink of beer
› a sudden forceful or unpleasant shake or movement

I or T: › [ I or T ] to shake or move someone or something unpleasantly or violently
› [ I or T ] If a sight, sound, or experience jars, it is so different or unexpected that it has a strong and unpleasant effect on something or someone.

I: › [ I ] to disagree or seem wrong or unsuitable

example: a jar of coffee/pickled onions
一罐咖啡／醃洋蔥
a jam jar
果醬罐子
We often have a jar or two at the pub after work.
我們經常在下班後到酒吧喝一兩杯啤酒。
With every jar of the carriage, the children shrieked with excitement.
車廂每劇烈震動一下，孩子就興奮地尖叫。
The sudden movement jarred his injured ribs.
突然的一個動作震痛了他受傷的肋骨。
The harsh colours jarred the eye.
這些強烈的色彩很刺眼。
A screech of brakes jarred the silence.
刺耳的煞車聲劃破了寧靜。
This comment jars with the opinions we have heard expressed elsewhere.
這個評論和我們在其他地方聽到的意見不一致。

NONE: › If something, especially a noise, jars on you, it annoys you.

example: His superior manner jars on me.
他那高高在上的樣子令我不快。
That squeaky voice is beginning to jar on me.
那尖細的說話聲開始讓我不舒服了。

NONE: › the amount that a jar can hold

example: The recipe uses a whole jarful/two jarfuls of jam.
這道菜要用一整罐／整整兩罐果醬。

NONE: C1 special words and phrases that are used by particular groups of people, especially in their work
